Review Title: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal
Review Content: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal. There seems to be a number of 'Amazon-qualified suppliers' involved. To know who you're buying from, the 'ships from/sold by' info. is on the right side of the product page. There may also be differences in packaging and accessories. Best to read through the advertising to know exactly what you're buying. Or contact the supplier before purchasing. Given that Amazon backs these purchases, not a concern. It arrived without scratches, dings, or apparent wear. Looks like new. That said, those buying a 'Renewed' phone should expect varying degrees of condition within the parameters of Amazon's advertising. I'd suggest buying a 'Renewed Premium' for your best chance of a like-new phone. I probably got lucky with a 'Renewed'. It shipped in a *very* well designed and protective box designed for phones. Not much larger than the boxes Apple packages iPhones in and similarly sturdy. Well suited for protecting the phone during shipping. If you plan on shipping your phone or storing a back-up, I'd suggest keeping it. The box has spacers to accommodate different sizes. Kudos to the packaging engineers. Well done. It was delivered with 100% battery health which almost certainly means that the phone was opened up and the battery replaced. The likelihood of a 'renewed' 13 Mini arriving with battery health at 100% is slim to none. I assume that they did this because the phone was traded in with < 80% battery health. Amazon advertising states that the phone will arrive with battery health of ≥ 80%. Notably, the battery was recognized by iOS as 'genuine' (thanks TECHMINT). Batteries that are not can lead to various issues, most importantly, safety issues. Look up "how to check if an iPhone battery is genuine". If it isn't, I'd suggest returning it to the supplier. Side note about iPhone battery replacement: If/when you have an iPhone battery replaced, I'd highly recommend scheduling it through Apple. Apple often contracts with third parties to do this in addition to Apple stores. When third parties sign up for this, they're held to a high standard and you're guaranteed to receive a 'genuine' battery. More importantly, if there's a problem you'll have the full weight of Apple behind you to resolve any issues. I'd also suggest reaching out to the supplier before purchase and asking what the battery health will be. In my experience with the iPhone 12 Mini, once you drop into the high 80% range, battery life becomes more noticeable. Note that Apple recommends replacing an iPhone battery when it reaches 80% battery health. I ran two diagnostics to check functions. In both cases, no issues. One of the diagnostics is built into iOS. You'll need iOS 17 or later and not a beta release. Search for 'built in iPhone diagnostic' for instructions. There's another which makes doing this quite a bit easier. From the Apple app store search for 'Phone Doctor Plus'. It's not a diagnostic as much as it's a function check but good for making sure everything works. There's a free and paid version. There are others but these are the only two I've tried. The advertising stated that an MFi certified charging/data cable ships with the phone. Mine shipped with a 3ft braided USB C to Lightning charging cable. No branding or print on the cable, no included documentation, no packaging. It appears similar to what you'll sometimes see without packaging and hanging from peg racks in convenience stores. I have no reason to believe that the provided cable isn't MFi certified and from a reliable manufacturer but without more information, best to use an Apple product or something from an established aftermarket supplier such as Belkin or Anker. Look for 'MFi certified' especially if you want fast charging capability. There are reasons USB C cables can be pricey, especially those designed for high power delivery. Mine shipped without a charger. I'd say the same about a charger as I did about the cable - MFi certified and from a reputable manufacturer - Apple, Belkin, Anker, etc. For the 13 Mini, Apple recommends a minimum of a 20 watt charger for optimal/fast charging . Apple's is about 20 dollars. It's also what Apple recommends for powering *the original* MagSafe accessory. The updated version of the MagSafe charger supports faster charging and according to Apple, a minimum of a 30 watt charger for optimal performance. Some suppliers advertise that a sim card removal tool is included. Mine didn't. If yours shipped with a sim card (mine did not), I'd suggest reading through the pros and cons of SIM vs eSIM. If eSIM meets your needs, I'd recommend removing the SIM and switching to eSIM. Switching to eSIM can be done in your phone's settings. No expertise or hardware required. Although unlikely if buying from an 'Amazon-qualified supplier' (I assume), SIM cards can be compromised. If you need a SIM card, best to get one from your carrier instead of a mystery SIM. The Apple leather case has been my go-to for the last 2-3 iPhones. Very well designed, doesn't add significant bulk, comfortable to grip, no sharp edges and it slips into and out of a pocket easily. The drop protection has proven to be excellent. Great case for all but extreme circumstances. They're relatively pricey so If you're looking to save, there are often Amazon customer returns available. eBay is another good source. The iPhone 12 mini and 13 mini cases are not interchangeable. I tried. The camera lens housings are different. The 12 mini case will not fit the 13 mini. The 13 mini case will fit the 12 mini but there will be a gap on the right side of the lens housing. Not to overstate it but If you're considering both the 12 mini and 13 mini, battery life may be problematic for heavy users. If you have a full size phone with a larger battery at ≥ 90% battery health (guesstimate) and often find yourself scrambling to find a charger, the Mini may not be for you. If you're on the move a lot without convenient charging options, a small power bank (≤ 5000mAh) will bring some peace of mind and a lot of convenience. Great when traveling. Definitely stick with time tested manufacturers. Anker and Belkin sell a wide variety. Note that the TSA only allows powerbanks in carry-ons. Apple discontinued it's iPhone power banks (Magsafe Battery Pack). As of this writing, you can still find them new from third party sources such as Walmart and eBay. Never buy used. There are confirmed and very convincing counterfeits out there so I'd be cautious about which supplier you choose. Look up "how to check if an Apple Magsafe Battery Pack is counterfeit". *Update* Apple reintroduced it's magsafe battery pack now called the iPhone Air MagSafe Battery. It was designed specifically for the iPhone Air and reportedly works with other iPhones - sort of. Not recommended. Fit issues. If you're looking at both the 12 and 13 Minis, the 13 Mini uses an A15 processor which is somewhat more energy efficient and slightly faster. It also has a ~10% larger battery. There are quite a few other differences including an upgraded camera. In day to day use, I found the differences to be negligible. I suspect that most people wouldn't be able to tell the difference without knowing what to look for. Definitely worth reading comparison reviews. Some of the updates will be important for some, less so for others. Search for "iPhone 13 mini vs iPhone 12 mini". If you read only one, Laptopmag.com published a well grounded, real-world comparison, no hype. Long term, the 13 Mini will receive system/feature updates from Apple for about a year longer. This may be the most value added difference. Generally speaking, Apple devices continue to receive security updates beyond the point that they are no longer supported with system/feature updates. Current estimates seem to be late 2027 for system/feature updates and 2030/2031 for security updates. When the security updates stop, best to replace the phone. If Apple's AI (Apple Intelligence) is a feature you want, it isn't supported in the Mini's. You can still use cloud based AI services but without the privacy and security features Apple bakes into it's AI. You'll need a minimum of an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max to use Apple's AI. Happy customer. I'm fully committed to the Mini form factor/dimensions. I carry it all day in a front or back pocket and barely know it's there. Having a phone with more screen, battery and features is nice but after the novelty wears off, having a phone that disappears into a pocket is more important for some of us. Sadly, not enough of us for Apple to justify continued production. When I need to replace it, perhaps Mini's will be back in the menu from Apple. Hope so. Review Title: ##### Well worth the money to go with Renewed Premium
Review Content: ##### Well worth the money to go with Renewed Premium. Edit to add: this is my 2nd phone I’ve bought from Amazon. My last phone (a renewed “good” SE 2nd gen) was bought at the end of 2022 and has been a reliable phone, I just wanted to upgrade and let the SE 2 (which after 3 years has 77% battery health) become my spare / back-up phone. I’m very happy with this seller & phone. Getting set up is proving challenging, but I’m thinking that’s an issue with my old phone & carrier that I’ll have to sort out after Christmas, not this phone itself so I’ll skip over the set up / switching from my old phone to this phone. (Edit: the issues I was having switching over from my old phone to this phone was I wasn’t paying attention to my account being locked to prevent unauthorized sim / phone number changes; once I went in my account and unlocked it, the switch went smoothly) Phone was shipped quickly (arrived the day after I ordered it) and arrived looking brand new, no scratches or scuffs, 98% battery health. (By contrast, I got my teenage daughter an iPhone 14 as well from another seller in “good” condition, her battery health was 87% which is still really good for a renewed phone) So far from what I’ve been able to tell with fairly limited use, I love the speed. It’s way faster than my SE 2 that I’m upgrading from. The battery holds charge pretty good. Since it had been charging during my set up & attempt to transfer from my old phone, it was at 100% so I unplugged it. 10 hrs later it’s at 96% (have used it some to take video and see what apps have successfully downloaded (transferred from iCloud because “transfer from another device” didn’t seem to be working—again very possible an issue with my old). (First initial charge to 100%, moderate use because I was still primarily using my SE2, battery lasted 36 hours 100% to 15%; now that everything has been switched over and I’m 100% using this phone, I’m expecting battery to be ok for all-day and ready to charge at night) — first full day of use near “typical” for me (took off charger around 5 AM, intermittent usage during the day; with no recharging during the day at 8:30 PM it was at 20%) After my experience with the SE 2 & the few days I’ve been using this 14, I will definitely be looking to buy my next phone on Amazon. Review Title: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking
Review Content: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking up where the prior phone handed off to the latest one. The challenge of course is you have a new phone - and its always a bit steep for the first few days trying to learn the new hardware/software and audit that the used phone does not have some hidden defect that is going to cost you more time and money. So, I'm happy for a few days and then one evening I discover that the bottom speaker (the top earpiece speaker is actually called the receiver) was not working well. scratchy and little to no volume - this had missed my attention entirely. A panic search online revealed Apple 12 speaker problems and them being repaired by Apple - crap! I went to a repair shop the next day, they ran Apple diagnostics on the phone and sure enough - speaker needed to be replaced - $120 for generic parts, $180 for Apple parts - they're not familiar with the Apple repair program (found out later that was for receiver speakers) - so this is half of the cost of the phone. No I'm committed to the new phone, don't want to lose it, but don't want to pay this either. Reach out to seller and explain the issue - they can even confirm the Apple diagnostic through the serial number - They offer $25 refund if I'll keep the phone. - So this tells me that they don't run diagnostics on the phones themselves - or do and hope that people will simply miss small items or accept them once they have sweat equity in the phone - or, it's all honest and by buying/selling a used phone both parties are taking a gamble. I chose to believe the latter. And accepted their offer. And here's the takeaway - the speaker now works - once in a while I might think I hear some scratchy, but unsure due to surrounding conditions. So for now, it's good, we'll see how long it lasts - but if I have to get it repaired - I took a chance - I say take a chance - you might get a perfect phone and save a lot in the meantime - I typically stay a few models behind the curve and benefit from software updates and people abandoning perfectly working phones for the latest models - AT&T typically had new old stock and I took advantage of that, but I have a grandfathered plan that they no longer make good money on, so I'm no longer eligible for that. Hope your experience is a good one - all the best, Don       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       216 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certifi
Review Content: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certified pre-owned” and ETC are all fancy wording for SECOND HAND, and USED. That said, with high hopes I purchased this device in May 2024 for my birthday, everything seemed to work fine, even though I noticed that the Maximum Battery Capacity was below 90%. —- Now in late January 2025 roughly only 8 months of use and the MBC has fallen to 77%, which has shown extreme degradation in that it cannot hold a charge. In addition, I have noticed that the touch screen is intermittent-Meaning that sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. Sometimes no have to press multiple times and extremely firm—Note that all softer is up to day on the iOS, as well as the Apps used. Also note that I have equipped this phone with a highend sturdy case, which has kept it well protected, although it has not suffered any falls or drops of any kind. Additionally, the screen is and has been protected and covered since the day I received the phone and it still intact with NO cracks or scratches —- All that said, aside from the disappointment of the battery not being at 99% when received and now not holding a charge through the day even with a mid day recharge, I am surprised that I could not get to at least a full 2 years before minor or even major hardware degradation had set in. The question then lies with the company who is selling the phones vs the Apple product itself. I can say ALL my Apple iPhone devices have held the test of time and I’ve never had to upgrade due to hardware, but due to obsoletion. SO, it is my assessment that the company selling the second hand item needs to do a better job checking the devices before resale, as well as fairly pricing it for its age and prior use.-not to mention changing the battery component if it is below 90%. The one, and only good thing I can say was the phone appeared relatively new with little evidence of use meaning just monor scratches on the metal chassis housing, although this goes completely unnoticed as the phone is covered completely with protection. The status of the companies integrity is still up for debate, if they can accommodate my request for a replacement to a newer iPhone model, for which I will pay the difference I will then say happy shopping to all customers, if not, I will say be WEARY of buying used, older model iPhone devices by smaller relatively unknown companies. Review Content: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certified pre-owned” and ETC are all fancy wording for SECOND HAND, and USED. That said, with high hopes I purchased this device in May 2024 for my birthday, everything seemed to work fine, even though I noticed that the Maximum Battery Capacity was below 90%. —- Now in late January 2025 roughly only 8 months of use and the MBC has fallen to 77%, which has shown extreme degradation in that it cannot hold a charge. In addition, I have noticed that the touch screen is intermittent-Meaning that sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. Sometimes no have to press multiple times and extremely firm—Note that all softer is up to day on the iOS, as well as the Apps used. Also note that I have equipped this phone with a highend sturdy case, which has kept it well protected, although it has not suffered any falls or drops of any kind. Additionally, the screen is and has been protected and covered since the day I received the phone and it still intact with NO cracks or scratches —- All that said, aside from the disappointment of the battery not being at 99% when received and now not holding a charge through the day even with a mid day recharge, I am surprised that I could not get to at least a full 2 years before minor or even major hardware degradation had set in. The question then lies with the company who is selling the phones vs the Apple product itself. I can say ALL my Apple iPhone devices have held the test of time and I’ve never had to upgrade due to hardware, but due to obsoletion. SO, it is my assessment that the company selling the second hand item needs to do a better job checking the devices before resale, as well as fairly pricing it for its age and prior use.-not to mention changing the battery component if it is below 90%. The one, and only good thing I can say was the phone appeared relatively new with little evidence of use meaning just monor scratches on the metal chassis housing, although this goes completely unnoticed as the phone is covered completely with protection. The status of the companies integrity is still up for debate, if they can accommodate my request for a replacement to a newer iPhone model, for which I will pay the difference I will then say happy shopping to all customers, if not, I will say be WEARY of buying used, older model iPhone devices by smaller relatively unknown companies. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 12 Pro, 128GB, Graphite - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller
Review Content: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller. It was roughly $200 more than the regular IPhone 12 that we bought for my son but it was the Pro model and it did have 512k of storage. Due to the positive experience we had with the earlier purchase, I decided to pull the trigger. Fulfillment was great. I had ordered the phone on 7/11 and it was scheduled to arrive on 7/14 but to my surprise it hit my house on 7/13 which was a nice surprise. When I picked up the package I got worried because I could hear and feel something rattling in the box that was shipped in a form fitting padded envelope. To my relief I found the phone to be intact. It arrived with protective plastic on the screen, a SIM port tool, and a lightning charging cable that was loose in the box. Upon inspection I found the screen to be free of scratches or gouges but there is some slight surface marring on a small section of the screen that you have to look for in order to see. The bezel was clean except for a couple of nicks. The worst sign of usage is a chip above the top of the highest camera lens. It’s not huge but you can definitely see it and it looks like a chip in a car windshield since the back of the phone is finished in glass. The only other thing to mention is that there was a bit of what looks like green metal tape that was poking out of the side of the phone between the screen and bezel which I was able to rub off with my fingernail. It looked like the refurb process was not as clean as it could have been. Going into the settings I found that the max battery life was only 85% which was kind of a bummer. Setting up the phone was a breeze with ICloud but I haven’t figured out how to pull down the pictures that resided on my old phone. My apps came over but know I had to re-enter my passwords in most cases. After only a couple of day usage, everything seems to work fine. Amazon gives 90 days to return for any issues. The camera on the pro is a definite improvement over the 7+. Size wise the unit is smaller than the 7+ but the screen is bigger on the 12 since it doesn’t have the home button at the bottom which I keep wanting to press out of habit. Overall the purchase was better than ok. If the phone has another 10% of battery life and the nick on the camera was not present then I would rate the item as excellent. I’ll always wonder if I should have purchased a phone from the other seller that sold a phone in perfect condition. I will update this review should anything major happen with the phone. Review Title: Comenzando por su diseño, el iPhone 12 Pro exhibe una estética elegante y sofisticada
Review Content: Comenzando por su diseño, el iPhone 12 Pro exhibe una estética elegante y sofisticada. Su construcción de vidrio y acero inoxidable le brinda una sensación de calidad y durabilidad, mientras que los bordes planos y la pantalla OLED sin bordes le dan un aspecto moderno y atractivo. Además, cuenta con la certificación IP68, lo que significa que es resistente al agua y al polvo, brindando tranquilidad en situaciones cotidianas. La pantalla Super Retina XDR de 6.1 pulgadas es simplemente impresionante. La resolución de 2532 x 1170 píxeles y la tecnología HDR permiten una reproducción de colores vibrante y contrastes intensos, lo que hace que ver contenido multimedia sea una experiencia gratificante. Además, la tecnología Ceramic Shield proporciona una mayor resistencia a caídas y arañazos, protegiendo la pantalla de posibles accidentes. El rendimiento del iPhone 12 Pro no se queda atrás. Equipado con el potente chip A14 Bionic de Apple y 6 GB de RAM, este dispositivo ofrece un rendimiento rápido y fluido en todas las tareas. Ya sea que estés navegando por la web, jugando juegos intensivos en gráficos o utilizando aplicaciones exigentes, el iPhone 12 Pro responde de manera ágil y eficiente. Además, la compatibilidad con la red 5G brinda velocidades de descarga y carga impresionantes, lo que hace que la experiencia en línea sea aún más satisfactoria. La cámara del iPhone 12 Pro es otro de sus puntos destacados. Con su sistema de triple cámara de 12 megapíxeles, que incluye un sensor principal, un ultra gran angular y un teleobjetivo, este teléfono te permite capturar imágenes y videos impresionantes en cualquier situación. La tecnología de estabilización de imagen óptica y el modo Noche mejorado hacen que las fotos con poca luz sean nítidas y detalladas. Además, la capacidad de grabar videos en calidad Dolby Vision HDR a 60 fps añade un nivel adicional de calidad cinematográfica a tus creaciones. En cuanto a la duración de la batería, el iPhone 12 Pro cumple con creces las expectativas. Su batería de iones de litio ofrece suficiente energía para todo el día de uso moderado, y la carga rápida de hasta 50% en 30 minutos es extremadamente conveniente cuando necesitas cargar el teléfono rápidamente. En resumen, el Apple iPhone 12 Pro de 128GB es un dispositivo impresionante en todos los aspectos. Su diseño elegante, rendimiento poderoso, pantalla deslumbrante y cámara de alta calidad se combinan para ofrecer una experiencia premium. Si estás buscando lo último en tecnología móvil y estás dispuesto a invertir en un dispositivo de gama alta, el iPhone 12 Pro es una opción que no te defraudará. Review Title: I have a series 4 that has been my main watch for a while, now
Review Content: I have a series 4 that has been my main watch for a while, now. It does most of what I need it to do, and it is reliable in the things it does well. But the battery life is not great, as you probably already know. I wanted a backup to wear while I charge it. I tried a cheaper alternative, but I have grown accustomed to certain features, so I got this series 6 to use alternately with my series 4. The "always on" display option might be helpful at work where I look at my watch often. when I synced to my phone, it gave me the option to use my current watch settings, so I did that, which was very convenient. However, both watches have the same name, now, which is less convenient. Not a deal breaker, however. It is disappointing that the spo2 has been disabled by apple. But again, not a deal breaker for me. I am more concerned about the heart rate monitoring, which works pretty well for my purposes. I will try the sleep monitoring, as well, to see if I find it useful. there are plenty of useful watch faces and I like that they can be customized to some extent. I have one for work, and a few others for personal use. I haven't used many other smart watches other than a fitbit, which became glitchy, especially in reading my heart rate. The apple watches have been reliable and work well with my iphone. So I decided to stick with what works for me. Review Title: Protected by the same 6-pack of snap-on protectors, the capabilities far outweigh the inconvenience
Review Content: Protected by the same 6-pack of snap-on protectors, the capabilities far outweigh the inconvenience of keeping a device on my wrist. I used to not wear a watch at all, for lack of utility, and lack of comfort. Elastic fabric bands, and cheap snap-on protectors have provided much more protection and convenience than their cost. The battery still gets me through a whole day, and charges in an evening between returning from work and going to bed. Apple needs to come out with something spectacularly better for me to care about upgrading. Firstly, I’ve never liked wearing a watch, especially because I don’t like most bands available. So this was a big leap of faith. As for value, $260 (at time of purchase) seems reasonable for a backup cellular device like this. There’s a 1x3mm scuff right beside one of the band-slots, but no functionality is hindered, and a case covers it. -no other negative quality issues are noticed (yet). -It gives me volume control on my AirPods Pro through, which is the only feature AirPods Pro are lacking in built-in features. -I’m able to get important info without spending time on my phone’s screen (reducing overall usage of screens in a day). -the alarm sounds are well-thought, and the vibration feels like someone is sweetly grabbing my wrist and gently wiggling it to wake me up. On that note, even for me, the watch (and the bands I bought in addition to the stock band) is comfortable enough to sleep in. -watch faces aren’t as diverse and artistic as I hoped, but they’re still decent. I have one that shows me the sun’s relative position in the sky on a time-scale of the day (one of the Solar Dial faces), which makes me think differently about chronologically when I am in my waking hours. -If you’re going to use it for a phone call, don’t lift your elbow high like an antenna to listen on the same side. Cross over your chest and use the opposite ear like a proper Starfleet cadet. -I’m not a wristwatch kind of person, neither am I particularly fashionable. But this is comfy, and the availability of 3rd party cases and bands make it easy to add an essence of expression to your daily demeanor. Review Title: I come from using a Samsung Active 2 and there are SO MANY more apps
Review Content: I come from using a Samsung Active 2 and there are SO MANY more apps. Apps that they both have work better too. For example on my samsung, I could only respond to a facebook message if someone sent me a message. On the Apple Watch 6 I can find the app on the list and view all the messages, even pictures! I love that you can handwrite responses. Voice input is better as well. ECG: I have atrial fibrillation, so that was my biggest reason for buying the watch. I bought the Samsung Active 2 because I suspected heart issues but we could never catch them. The ECG on Samsung worked only when you put your finger on it. It often was really picky about the pressure you put on it resulting in lots of reading errors and artifacts. I switched to Apple because many other afib people said it can detect and alert you to an episode. I haven't had an alert yet but I think my afib is under control at the moment. Still, it gives much cleaner ECGs with almost no artifacts. Doesn't do the crazy up and downs that Samsung did if you didn't keep the pressure perfect when taking a measurement. The amount of health data that can be tracked is unreal. I was able to link my patient charts from my doctors which shows and takes into account health data. I have continuous glucose monitoring and log my readings in it also. It even links up with my pokemon go so much better. I'm super happy with this purchase. I saw it as an investment in my health and I got on top of that so many great additions that I didn't realize I was missing on Android/Samsung. I am now an Apple convert. Review Title: Upon arrival, I was satisfied with the phone despite the phone having much more extensive screen wea
Review Content: Upon arrival, I was satisfied with the phone despite the phone having much more extensive screen wear than expected AND a pretty poor excuse for a screen protector meant to cover up the screen wear. It is however an old model, refurbished phone, so that is to be expected. Upon receiving the iphone I promptly turned it on and tested the device, including the battery life. 91%. Given they guarantee 80% I thought I got really lucky and hit the refurbished jackpot. Well, fast forward not even a week and I decided to check the battery life again. 82%???? Now I am no engineer, but 9% battery degradation in less than a week sounds excessive. I figured its still above 80%(what was advertised) so I still got the product I payed for. I can live with a shorter battery life. Fast forward 7 more months of minimal use. The phone is on daily with very limited screen time. Work related texts and calls. Occasionally audible, or spotify use. Monitored all my charging to prevent over charging. Im not sure what rate of degradation is normal but given my use case mine seems to have died unreasonably quickly. I bought this as a cheaper alternative to a new iphone but 300 is by no means cheap and for a device that is quickly dying 8 months later. I am always a bit nervous buying refurbished tech, especially from Amazon. Buying refurbished is a flip of a coin and you may get luckier than me but this left a sour taste in my mouth and left me feeling inclined to leave this review as a disclaimer. In the future I will either buy new, or go the ebay refurbished route given their refurbs tend to be a bit cheaper and come with a 1 year warranty on all ebay certified refurbished tech. Good luck to all those in the market. If you decide to go this route, I hope you get luckier than I did. As you move, choose from a variety of music, podcasts, and audiobooks to entertain and motivate you. For added fun, share your activity rings with friends and challenge them to 7-day activity competitions. Throughout the day, the Apple Watch SE keeps you connected with the world around you. When paired with your iPhone, you can make calls and send texts directly from your wrist, navigate your surroundings with Maps, buy items with Apple Pay, and use your voice to interact with Siri. Made to last in almost any kind of weather, the Apple Watch SE is water-resistant up to 164'. Use its 32GB of built-in storage for apps, watch faces, music, and more. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 17 Pro, US Version, 256GB, eSIM, Deep Blue- Unlocked (Renewed Premium) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### Scary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced it
Review Content: ##### Scary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced it I had not purchased an Amazon Refurbished product before. But we were looking for a large capacity 1TB iPhone 17 Pro, and didn't find one available for under $1300 + tax at local Apple Stores. With the new iPhones coming out at the end of the summer, we didn't want to pay full price, but our old iPhone was full and wasn't working very well. So, during Prime Day sales, we decided to order a Renewed Premium iPhone 17 Pro 1TB from Amazon. It wasn't available for next day or 2 day delivery, but the priced was great under $1300. When delivery came, I was waiting by the front door like a little kid during Christmas. I opened the Amazon box showing 2 items inside and I grabbed the Renewed Premium box and there was no shrink wrap, no sealed close tape to prevent the box from being opened. In my hast, I didn't even record the box opening process. I just flipped open the lid and was shocked to find an empty box with just a charge cable and no iPhone 17 Pro. I looked at the Amazon outside brown box to check for tampering, looked good, one layer of table, not cut open and resealed. I called Amazon Customer service immediately, she said the driver made a mistake and would deliver it the following day (a weekend delivery). My order showed as delivered. - about $1300 and all I had was an emplty box with a USB-C charge cable. That's it. Did I just make the biggest mistake on this on-line order? Why didn't I. record opening the box? I felt bad, and thought driver error??? No way, the outside brown box was sealed. The refurbished box had to have been tampered with in the packing and shipping stage, not during the delivery. I called Amazon Customer Service again, explaining the empty box. They asked for photos which I took shortly after the delivery. They agreed to send a replacement. We got the replacement and were quite happy with it's like new quality. No signs of use, no nics or scratches and it's battery was at 100% capacity with I think 1 cycle on it. Amazon came through with a great replacement. It took several hours to restore and then add it to our account. But all works great now. So, it was a little scary with no product in an empty box, but Amazon Customer Service (my second - third calls) did fix the order and it was a great deal. Look at the refurbished details carefully, and video opening the box and the package contents so you have some evidence on what was was actually in the box. Especially if it is not shrink wrapped or sealed with tape. My video of the replacement didn't show the shrink wrapping well in the photo grab of the opening of the shrink wrap. Thanks to my 2nd and 3rd contact of Customer Service to resolve this purchase. And PS the iPHone 17 Pro is awesome and has lot so space to record kids and concerts. Review Title: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here
Review Content: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway. I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering. The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after. The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced. I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there. So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use. RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I run and used to track my progress with my iPhone but I don’t really like carrying with me
Review Content: I run and used to track my progress with my iPhone but I don’t really like carrying with me. I have had this happen a few times and caused the watch to fall off onto the floor. I’m not too worried about this as I plan on replacing the band when I find one I like. It is really clever and easy to remove the bands for replacement. Nice engineering on that. I don’t really use much of the other apps other than fitness or weather and of course time. But there are many and with the large screen they are easy to use and the interface easy to navigate. When it comes time to replace the watch I am sure I will purchase another Apple Watch, though I am uncertain if it will be new since I had good luck with this renewed purchase. Review Title: I want to keep my earbuds in for the whole journey, and these are the one good quality sounding earb
Review Content: I want to keep my earbuds in for the whole journey, and these are the one good quality sounding earbuds I can find to achieve that. They have a flat battery close to the jack plug, with a power switch and charging port. All international aircraft now have USB ports in them, so I just plug in a power cable and can listen through them for 10 hours or more while enduring the pleasure of flying. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 6 (GPS, 44mm) - Blue Aluminum Case with Deep Navy Sport Band (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: This watch is incredible
Review Content: This watch is incredible. I have done the following since having the watch: Outdoor work (chopping wood, cleaning a nasty chicken coop, setting up a treestand) I’m sure there is more but I wanted to emphasize I’ve done A LOT with this watch. I also did a run on the beach but I took the watch off when going in the ocean. I possibly didn’t need to but salt water is just so corrosive I didn’t want to risk it. This watch has performed flawlessly the entire time. I’m more than impressed. My son bought one of these new when they first came out and paid double what I paid. My cons list is short: (and really not the seller but the watch itself) I didn’t realize if you have a tattoo where the sensor sits it will not read correctly. I thought something was wrong with my watch but did a little research and found it was the tattoos on my wrist…I verified this by moving the watch to an area with then without and watching the watch shut off. I now choke the watch up a little closer to my hand (which can be annoying sometimes when working out) and it works perfectly. Also…I think sunscreen might affect the sensor as well. I had sunscreen on and the watch was doing a similar thing that it did with the tattoo. I wiped the sensor and my wrist off and it started working fine. Lastly I do wish the watch came with a little better charger…the one they sent me works just fine but it’s slow as can be. The charger my son has charges our watched in 1.5-2 hours. Overall…everything I’ve said below is just as (if not more) relevant. I wouldn’t hesitate to buy this watch again. I’m extremely satisfied. I would have shared a picture or 2 but amazon asked permission to all my pictures and that isn’t happening. I’m writing this knowing I’ve only had the watch for 3 days. I plan to update my review before the 90 day return runs out and after I’ve had more time with the watch. I got this watch specifically from seller prime mobility. They have very high feedback ratings so I was happy to take a chance with them in this watch. I bought the watch in “like new” condition. The seller was prompt with shipping and communication. At this point I would recommend them highly. I did a lot of research on what watch to get for fitness and overall health. It seems with all my research, for people who aren’t super techy and have an iPhone the Apple Watch is the way to go. I’ve never owned an apple or any other smart watch/smart device. I wanted this to track my 5 day a week gym workouts, sleep, and heart rate with running, meditation, and cold plunging. I honestly only have 1 con at this point. The watch came with a sticker right on the health tracker and the glue was annoying (really not hard just annoying) to have to remove. The pros are many: the watch came with %100 battery health witch I was surprised about. I’ve been using it and I’ve only had to charge it every 1.5 days. It also looks great. No visible issues, problems, blemishes at all. Lastly, the first day I had it I did a 10 minute cold plunge. The watch was under water for 10 minutes and had no issues. The watch quality meets my expectations completely and even exceeded them regarding battery life. I’m incredibly happy with my purchase. I can’t speak for other sellers but I feel prime mobility did me well in this purchase. Again, I will be updating my review before the 90 day return runs out but at this point I don’t have any concerns or apprehensions. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 6 (GPS, 44mm) - Blue Aluminum Case with Deep Navy Sport Band (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: Battery life - Better than anticipated
Review Content: Battery life - Better than anticipated. Apple promises 24hrs, I’m seeing more than 36hrs. Resolution - V good. Sharp & clear. Better than a lot of friends watches. Touch sensitivity- Excellent. Accurate (even on the smallest of icons/text). V responsive and no lag no matter how quick or lightly u touch it. Brightness - V good. I haven’t had it fade-out in the Florida sun and can always read it. Fitness tracker - Excellent. The native work out app has multiple modes (gym, tennis, rowing, cycling) and can detect what activity ur doing. It displays pulse, active calories and total calories. Health tracker - Excellent. The watch comes w blood oxygen monitoring, heart rate monitoring and more. I’ve only used the HR & BO and have found the pair to be accurate. Additionally, the latter have helped me fine tune some eating habits as I wasn’t aware how much certain foods affected my HR & BO. Sleep monitor - V Good. I’ve found this has helped me drive towards a better nights sleep. Apps - Excellent. Apple Watch has more apps than u can shake a stick at, and they work well. Apple Pay - Excellent. The convenience of using ur watch over fumbling for a wallet or phone is off the charts. Additionally, it works perfectly. Telephone calls - Excellent. Receiving and making calls is a breeze and has worked flawlessly. I never expected to use this feature but the watch speaker is loud/clear and the person at the other can’t tell I’m calling from an external device. This is especially impressive since the call is relayed through my iPhone. Texting - Excellent. The Siri/dictation features are excellent. I can send receive texts flawlessly (no more phone fumbling) and the manual input works flawlessly too. The only drawback is u can’t select emojis but if u say “happy face”, Siri will insert the latter in character form. Setup - It’s pretty much a breeze. Charge the watch, download the Apple watch app to ur phone. Put the watch by the phone and follow the instructions. Any apps that can b transferred from ur phone will be transferred. Usefulness - Off the charts. This is not so much a watch but a miniature digital Swiss Army knife. The watch is unobtrusive and having so many of our daily digital-needs on a wrist makes life a lot easier. There r a lot more features to suit how u would use it. I thought I would find the short battery life a nuisance, not at all. Plus I don’t use the watch everyday….at times my wrist will go commando or I’ll wear a real watch to mix it up. I would recommend purchasing a protective case for it….the one I have is a chrome silicon thingy that protects against scratches, dings and has a raised lip to protect the screen. I am so glad I gave this ‘6’ a try before purchasing a 7. The leap between the two is marginal (despite what the marketing dept would have u believe). V happy w purchase and hope to keep the device for a long time.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: the airpods came in the official packaging and had everything from the box to the instructions to th
Review Content: the airpods came in the official packaging and had everything from the box to the instructions to the charging cable. the box was pretty obviously worn and a little dirty, but it was nothing major. the airpods and case looked clean, but because of covid, i wiped them both down anyway (along with everything else). there was no earwax on the airpods, nor anything else dirtying the case. the charging cable was not only in perfect condition, but it was also tied into a neat coil at the bottom of the box with plastic, which was quite nice. it works perfectly. i also realized it was also a lightning cable and could be used interchangeably with my regular charging cable, so i could charge my phone when i wasn’t charging the case and vice versa. it’s also handy if a second charging cable would be convenient; in my case, i decided to keep the new cable plugged into my computer across the room from my old cable so i could charge either my phone or my airpod case no matter where i was in my room. the airpods seem to work perfectly fine as well. i’ve never had airpods prior to these, so i don’t have anything to compare them, but the case and airpods charge properly, i’ve had no connectivity issues so far, and while i’m no audiophile, the sound quality seems fine too. and my little monkey brain is *very* satisfied by how the case’s lid snaps open and shut. i could fidget with it all day. it’s kinda loud when snapping shut, but very nice. overall, i’m very satisfied with my product! i’m surprised at the quality because this is a used item (mine even had the name of the previous owner) but i don’t regret my purchase at all! if you want somewhat cheap airpods, this is your best shot! The watch feels responsive, and navigating menus is smooth with no lag or performance issues. The 44mm size strikes a nice balance between screen space and comfort. The display is easy to read, whether I'm checking messages, tracking workouts, or glancing at the weather. The Midnight aluminum case and matching sport band also give it a clean, modern look that works well for both casual and professional settings. Battery life has been consistent throughout the day. I typically wear it from morning until bedtime for activity tracking, notifications, and occasional workouts, and I still have battery remaining at the end of the day. Charging overnight has become part of my routine. One of the biggest benefits has been the fitness and health tracking. Activity rings, step counts, heart rate monitoring, and workout tracking provide useful information without being complicated. It has helped me stay more aware of my daily activity levels. Battery health may vary slightly between renewed units Does not include some premium features found on higher-end Apple Watch models Overall, the Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) delivers a great smartwatch experience at a more affordable price point. If you're already in the Apple ecosystem and want reliable notifications, fitness tracking, and everyday convenience, the renewed version is an excellent value and performs much like a new device. Review Title: Pairing to my iPhone 15 was as simple as placing the watch next to the iPhone, with Blue tooth enabl
Review Content: Pairing to my iPhone 15 was as simple as placing the watch next to the iPhone, with Blue tooth enabled, and following on-screen instructions. The watch did require updating the iOS to 26 before pairing could be completed. So, don't be in a hurry to use the watch after you receive. Give it time to update and pair. The watch did come with a new band, and a wireless charger with USB C connector. I have already taken advantage of the many health features of the Apple Watch. It's been great so far. If I am to dock any points off this purchase, it will be 0.5 pts for the wireless charger. It seems to be low Wattage as it took about 4 hours or more to first charge the watch. I was using a power block rated 35 watts, so it wasn't my power supply. I recommend to anyone buying an Apple watch to purchase a screen protector of some type. I also recommend purchasing a wireless charger with higher output. I did end up purchasing a 22W 3 in 1 wall charger with built-in magnetic Wireless charger for Apple watches. The wireless charger is rated 2.5 Watts, and it charges the Apple Watch SE much quicker than the corded charger provided with the watch. Review Content: Mine came almost like new condition. Super happy with it so far. Had a SE prior to this one which the screen broke on, this one I have a screen protector for. I’d definitely recommend going with one as the screen replacement would have cost me the same or more then upgrading with a newer refurbished model. Definitely pleased with my purchase/shape it came sent to me. (Had a recent bump in the road where the watch did find itself stuck and unable to take a charge). I’m not sure why, but after the 20th or so attempt at resetting it in which this time I held both the crown and button down for well over 1 minute, the screen finally reappeared & it looks as though it will begin charging once again. The battery life on it has not been the “best” so to say, but it certainly did not make sense for it to go from lasting a full day to just dying completely. Right now fingers crossed since it finally got off of the screen that shows the charging cable with the green light lit to showing the time, I’m hopeful it will now take a proper charge once again and work correctly. If that’s the case I certainly stand by my 5 star review for the value I received buying this refurbished. My tip to those who run into battery issues is to just keep messing around with it. Make sure of course the proper charging Amps are being used & for some strange reason the very long hold on both buttons along with just some random reset tries I’ve given the watch-hooray it finally looks like my watch is going to hold a change again. 🙂. Review Title: Everything seemed to be going well when I got the item
Review Content: Everything seemed to be going well when I got the item. It is in fantastic external condition, but within the first day, I realized that the battery would not hold charge. I inspected it after it happened the second day and found that the battery capacity is significantly degraded, down to almost 70%. This is refurbished, so I definitely don’t expect 100%, but I think it’s reasonable to expect 85% or above. What is the point of having this watch if I can’t even wear it long enough for it to get a read before I have to charge it again? Then, four days after its arrival, the side button started malfunctioning. It kept showing the “emergency services” screen when it was just sitting on the nightstand, constantly. The screen showed that the little side icon for the button was held down, even though the button was not stuck at all. This led me to shut the entire thing down every night so that it wouldn’t accidentally call the police! The two days after that, the screen suddenly went black (full charge) and the device entered an infinite boot loop. Just the Apple logo, black screen, Apple logo… etc. every ten seconds. It will not turn on or off, it will not hard reset or force reset. I’ve watched every video. I chatted with Apple support (where Amazon sent me to solve the issue, strangely), who told me it would cost almost $400 to fix the watch. Why on earth would I do that? Review Title: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking
Review Content: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking. There's no such thing as the simple pinch & zoom on it. That particular luxury seems to be found only within the Camera & Picture sections. You'd think it'd at least be within the iBook section but it's not. On most everything Windows or Google, every app is not just touch & activate, but also affords the luxury of pinch & zoom as well as easy swipe & easy app close & dismiss. Can't say that about the Apple iPhone. And for some unknown reason its WiFi also keeps turning itself on. I can't seem to keep it off no matter how often I manually turn it off. For Apple being so USER-FRIENDLY, I cannot at all say that it is. In fact, IT IS ANYTHING BUT USER-FRIENDLY. If the Apple World was so user-friendly, then it would be a very simple and easy transition from the Windows or Google platform to Apple. And I can honestly say it is Not at all simple or easy. I was so hoping it would be as simple & easy as my Windows machine & Android phone, but sadly, it's actually quite maddening. If you enjoy Kindle reads, you'll need to install the app for it. But I can also tell you, Apple's iBook seriously pales in comparison to Kindle. Ironically, the Google Search Engine is installed on Apple's iPhone but Kindle is not. I avoid Google anything & everything as much as can be done. But for Apple to deny Amazon's Kindle Apple on its phones, seems almost a crime. I have yet to install the Kindle reading app or to test out the camera on the iPhone. When I do I'll update my review. But currently I can't say it's anything to brag about. And I most certainly did not expect to see Google's Search Engine/Web Browser on it. Size wise, it's the exact same size as my Sony Xperia Z3v. It still functions quite well. Not perfect, but well enough for me since I have it locked to call, text, Kindle reads & camera. I can easily read, pinch & zoom & highlight my Kindle reads, pictures & text messages on it. Can only do that with pictures on the iPhone. So for it being so great, I actually find it quite limiting. Not because it's an iPhone, but because the Apple creators decided to create a platform that is quite complex and extremely arduous to use. Review Content: I’m writing this review a bit late as i got the phone around the time 17 of February after purchasing on the 7th. I also live a caribbean country so returning this would have been so much more costly than to keep it if anything was wrong with it. I even contacted the seller to let them know my concern (to which they answered, God bless electronics deals❤️) Buttt! the phone came in amazing quality! the battery health is at 100% as shown in the picture, the touch responsiveness is about as smooth as a new iphone and the exterior of the phone is in good condition. a few scratches on stainless steel sides of the phone but nothing too serious, also 2 scratches on the screen but barely noticeable from 12ft away or using a screen protector, it doesn’t affect the screen quality so everything’s fine there. The camera works beautifully no faulty there, the speaker, silencer button everything working great! I’m even writing this review using the phone right now🥰 The phone however, came in a white small phone looking like box, covered in bubble wrap. Not sure if i was lucky or if they do this to all the phones but, mine came with a case and screen protector already on! I later swapped them out for a different phone case and privacy screen protector. The charger however was 3rd party (lighting cable to type A) luckily i bought a new one prior and one of my friends gave me an authentic apple charger (the phone now charges to 100% within 45 mins) To sum it up, I definitely recommend! the worst case is that your battery health is below 90% or you can be lucky to get 100% battery health like me! either way you be saving a ton of money (an iphone 13 pro usually goes for about 1500-1650 EC in my country however, i bought this phone at the time for 950 EC, definitely a steal.) thank you so much electronic deals, super happy. Review Title: After much research, I decided to choose Amazon's refurbished program over Apple, Best Buy, or Walma
Review Content: After much research, I decided to choose Amazon's refurbished program over Apple, Best Buy, or Walmart. My phone is essential for so many reasons - work, communication with aged parents on-call emergencies, and so much more. Amazon should be ashamed of calling a product "Refurbished Excellent", when it falls apart after only a few months of use! Over $400, and now it will take more than that to repair! Review Title: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro
Review Content: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro... and - because of last year's experience - went elsewhere first. What I got from them this time was definitely not what I ordered (it was supposed to be "pristine"... what I got was scratched up junk). So I came back to Amazon, and ordered the only "used-like new" offering on the i13 Pro "list" that day. What I got, well, wasn't (i.e., wasn't "used-like new"). Again. Sigh. (I have a ton of experience with buying "used-like new" stuff from Amazon over the years, and I know what to expect... and this wasn't it.) What I received was a "refurbished-excellent" i13 Pro (the same category as the i13 I ordered last year... which was again, anything but, back then, lol). The category which is is now listed on the order form. (Why would they change the category? When it wasn't what I ordered? -Dunno.) It was... almost... perfect: a few tiny scratches around the lightning port is all a minute examination found wrong (the previous owner had mostly used mag-charging I imagine). And... the battery health - while entirely within the spec for Amazon refurbished (i.e., "80% or greater") - was still a disappointment at only 84%. Still. Cosmetic-wise... acceptable. More than acceptable, even. Agreeably nice... obviously: as I kept it. (Note: I wouldn't review it if I hadn't kept it.) Note: For long term use of any iPhone, to avoid battery related issues, Apple recommends replacing the battery when its below 80% battery health... which repair cost from Apple is about $90 or so... iow, not a big deal. Look, I'm not the target demographic for a new Apple phone anyways; especially their Pro. So sending the phone in for a new battery, especially for what I paid for the 1TB version, is a-okay. And figured into the price. But - other than battery health... and those few tiny [mostly unnoticeable] scratches - I paid quite a bit less (saved a couple of hundred over the "other guys" offerings) at Amazon for a truly ultra-clean i13 Pro - with 1TB capacity - which is in otherwise almost perfect condition. And while its minor flaws render it most certainly NOT in the "used-like new" category... the savings over market costs for a 1TB version rendered my objections to the category moot: it was more than good enough as "refurbished-like new" lol. While YMMV, well... after all... in the final analysis... this one is a keeper. Just keep in mind: all refurb's are "luck of the draw". Amazon is great about their return policy. Take a chance. You'll save money... maybe a bunch of money. Final word: recommend. Review Title: The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tow
Review Content: The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tower connectivity, whereas the 14 and newer also have SOS and roadside assistance functionality via satellite. Based on where I live (mountains, bad cell coverage) I was torn between this purchase and the iPhone 14 Pro series, especially after I realized that a third party seller here on Amazon was offering a "excellent condition" renewed model for what I paid for this older model. Having said this, the iPhone Pro 14 has had reports of overheating and/or lackluster battery performance compared to the iPhone 13 Pro. I also like the fact that the iPhone 13 Pro does NOT have the "always on" screen common to newer Pro models. Another notable difference is that the iPhone 13 Pro (and earlier) have a physical SIM tray whereas the newer 15 Pros are eSIMs. Finally, the iPhone Pro 13 and earlier uses a lightening cord vs. USB-C on current-generation iPhones. (I'm not interested in using a different charging cord/setup than my spouse, especially while traveling.) I very much appreciate the excellent cosmetic appearance — there were no scratches or gouges to be found anywhere on the phone I received — but keeping the Pro 13 was not an option. In a video I took of a flock of birds flying just after the sun set behind a hillside, I could make out a round dust spot visible against the cloudless, pale gold sky — dead center in the bottom of the frame (landscape mode). Honestly, I probably never would have seen it in broad daylight because the HDR takes the blue sky and darkens it down so much the dust spot would have been masked — but the light I was shooting against at dusk was just a tad bit paler than the dust spot, allowing me to appreciate that the lenses were not in the perfect shape they initially appeared. Upon further inspection, using a flashlight, I noted some kind of residue *behind* two out of the three lenses. (Supposedly these lenses are sealed but per the reviews here mine is not the first report of dust spots in photos.) Overall, I don't feel like I received the "premium renewed" experience, in part because the shipping was slow (nearly four days before Amazon assigned tracking) and battery health was less than expected (others here reported at or near 100%!). Ultimately, I returned the Pro 13 and bought an iPhone Pro 12 from another seller. Not only did I pay less and end up with a slimmer, lightweight phone that feels better in the hand, but I actually like the camera quality better because it is among a very small number of iPhones where it is actually possible to turn off the HDR. Review Title: I initially bought two of these
Review Content: I initially bought two of these. One for me and my 9 year old but had to return the second pair because I previously bought iwatches from a different seller. I was told they are lost in transit after two weeks so I went ahead and get these from Amazon. Lo and behold, those lost watches arrived while this order is in transit. The seller told me to keep the watches but when these arrived, my son decided that he doesn’t want the starlight watch and wants this shiny black one. lol Anyway, I only activated one of them and had to return the other. As per usual.. the initial set up takes forever but after all that step, the watch works well. As you can see, the battery is 100% capacity. Appearance: theres minimal scratches but nothing that stands out or can be considered as an eyesore . Connection: I have yet to turn on the cellular data on this thing so I can’t say anything about that yet but as far as WiFi.. it connects well. My son used it a lot last night to play with the walkie talkie. Messages sent through WiFi arrives fast.. so are the calls. Speaker and microphone works well. Features: As mentioned, my son absolutely loves the walkie talkie app. He was sending both me and his Dad some texts using the WiFi connectivity. Made calls. It’s set up as a kid account so there’s limited features in there than you would usually have as an adult. As a parent though.. I love that it has a school time feature that allows me to lock his watch whenever he is in school. Actually, I like ALL of the parental controls in this thing. Durability: it’s made of ionX glass. While it claims to be durable, it is still made out of glass. It can scratch easily and will shatter with impact. As this is set up as a child watch.. I went ahead and bought him a protective case. The watch band that came with it is a little flimsy but you can always get new ones here anyway.. and cheap. The charger cord that came with it is a USB-A which has its pros and cons. USB-A is still very popular and can come in handy especially when traveling. however, it charges slower than USB-C chargers. If that is something you don’t want to deal with, you can always buy a better charger here. Overall, he is very happy with this watch. It looks almost brand new, works well, function as it should be. Review Title: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100
Review Content: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100 more than the renewed price but for that you get an item whose battery is at least at 90% capacity relative to a new one and instead of a 90 day warranty you get a year warranty and a year to return the item. For less than $100 I thought that was definitely worth it. However the first iPhone 12 pro they sent me had a battery that was at 85% capacity which really pissed me off because I felt cheated so I returned it and purchased it again and I'm glad I did because the 2nd ones battery was at 100% capacity and for all intents and purposes it was a brand new phone at a used price. Granted it's still really expensive it was $900 before tax but I got this to be future proof at least for the next several years. This is my first iPhone before I was all android phones but it seemed like every year I was having to buy another phone because something out of my control always happened but my parents still had their iPhone 8 that they bought new and it was still working perfectly. I haven't had this phone for more than a few days but so far I'm very impressed with it. The facial recognition capabilities are so good. My phone can recognize me when I'm in a dark room whereas my Samsung tablet can't recognize my face without all the lights on. One feature this phone doesn't have that really surprised me was that there is no built in fingerprint scanner and I think that was a mistake on apple's part. The battery is supposed to only last 21 hours but a full charge is lasting me a little over 2 days. The screen is gorgeous is it HDR Dolby Vision and HLG compatible and not even my 4k tv supports all of those so it makes streaming look brilliant. You can see every detail even though the screen is 6.7inches. it seems like everyday I'm finding out a new function that this phone has granted a lot them I'll never use because I don't use my phone that way but it's cool to know that if I wanted to I could if I so choosed. I guess I'll stop my review here because you get the gist and I hate it when people on Amazon beat a dead horse and I don't want to be one of those so Amazon renewed premium is a worthwhile program and the iPhone 12 pro max is an awesome phone that's worth the investment. Review Title: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter
Review Content: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter. We don't believe in buying $1,000+ phones for teenagers. Amazon's Refurbished was a welcomed gift! The phone comes well packaged and is in great shape. It works like new, as promised! But, it took us MANY HOURS to finally get this phone set-up and info transfered over. Here are some learned tips for set-up: First, fully charge the new phone and your old phone. If possible, leave them both plugged in during the process. We learned that your old phone needs to be at least 50% charged before it will even start the transfer process. Don't bother backing up your old phone to the iCloud beforehand. It's much faster to wait and do that with the new phone after all is said and done. Your first step, go into the new phone and in Settings, go into General, then update the software to the latest version. We had many issues with the process stalling and then we would finally get an error message? This wasted a lot of time! It's so much quicker to update that software first, though it will take awhile (not lying). Once the software on the new phone is updated, then start the transfer process with your old phone. It will take a while (maybe 30 minutes). Once the whole thing transfers, your new phone will work and everything on the screen will look like your old phone. Here's the one thing we did not think about, you will still need a new SIM card from your Carrier. They are free. Simply go to your Carrier's store and explain that you bought a used phone and they will give you one. After everything is all set-up, call your carrier with your old phone and they will talk you through the process of installing the new SIM into the new phone. They will even test it out with you online until it works. Amazon Refurbished is guarranteed and definitally cheaper than other sites. The phone arrives fast too! After all is said and done, wipe the old phone to factory settings and remove the SIM card. Then you are all set! Newer phone at a cheaper price, it's guarranteed, and my daughter is totally happy with it! [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Review Title: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected
Review Content: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected. My phone was put into what seemed like a generic Android phone box, which, I’ll let you know damn near gave me a heart attack when I opened. Inside were a few things. An Amazon renewed card and one other thing I can’t remember- as well as the phone (obviously) and a charger and charging brick. Charger and charging brick are standard but the cable feels pretty nice and the brick is a good size. Standard plastic holder inside. Nothing more, nothing less. No complaints. For the actual phone, it was inside of a plastic zip bag. The bag itself was scratched up so it was difficult to see the phone inside until i took it out. The first thing I did when I took it out was inspect it for damage. I was completely ready to pack it back up and send it back- but I was pleasantly surprised. The phone had very little cosmetic damage, just some scratches on the frame (my case covers it anyways, so it doesn’t matter to me) and literally no screen damage- besides a little scratch on the upper right corner near the bezel. And you have to remember these phones are used, so I didn’t feel a need to dock a star for that, since you can only see the scratch when the screen is off and light is being reflected onto it. Overall, 9.5/10 for cosmetics. Then, the battery. My particular phone came with 80% battery health, which I personally don’t mind. I have the means to be able to get it replaced when the time comes, and to be honest was a relief after my last IPhone 11 from another seller had 100% battery health, just for it to be a non-Apple battery and cause all sorts of problems. Overall, I have no complaints with this phone. It’s in great condition in my book. Mic, speakers, cameras, haptics, everything (as far as I’ve been using it) has been in perfect order. Based on other reviews, whatever phone you get from this seller honestly depends on luck. It’s trivial, and that should never be the case, but if you can, I’d say take the risk. Worse case scenario you return it and get a full refund and try again. Overall, I’m very happy with my purchase. Review Title: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine
Review Content: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. After a week and a half of going round and round with our phone carrier, we finally figured out the phone was not fully unlocked as the listing had set. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”! The phone is slender not heavy but a case did help tremendously holding it cause it’s so thin.. haha i dont know how to explain that one but I Dont know to drop it haha so a case helps to grip it .. if that makes sense ? Lol But with the cheaper price tag ? I was able to get the highest GB and still save a few hundred’ dollars! I did my research cause I was looking at this phone for a while and then was gearing for the 12 pro Max for it has 3 or 4 better features. But After comparing and deep research? What was being said is true! The 11’s are amazing phones! And unless your a Photographer? You won’t see a inkling of a difference with the camera or video.. the processor in the 11’s are also fast and made right! Apple surly did a great job with the 11’s !!! So again for what you get and with that price tag ? You can’t go wrong with the Iphome 11 pro Max! I’m freaking happy I got one heck of a deal ! I love the look ,the quality, how fast it responds, the pictures, the battery life, the features, and the company that I bought it from! Hope this helps with someone’s research and decision making! Review Content: Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%. Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended. Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars. Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered. Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%. Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up. Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only. Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars.
