Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 13 Mini, 128GB, Midnight - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal
Review Content: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal. There seems to be a number of 'Amazon-qualified suppliers' involved. To know who you're buying from, the 'ships from/sold by' info. is on the right side of the product page. There may also be differences in packaging and accessories. Best to read through the advertising to know exactly what you're buying. Or contact the supplier before purchasing. Given that Amazon backs these purchases, not a concern. It arrived without scratches, dings, or apparent wear. Looks like new. That said, those buying a 'Renewed' phone should expect varying degrees of condition within the parameters of Amazon's advertising. I'd suggest buying a 'Renewed Premium' for your best chance of a like-new phone. I probably got lucky with a 'Renewed'. It shipped in a *very* well designed and protective box designed for phones. Not much larger than the boxes Apple packages iPhones in and similarly sturdy. Well suited for protecting the phone during shipping. If you plan on shipping your phone or storing a back-up, I'd suggest keeping it. The box has spacers to accommodate different sizes. Kudos to the packaging engineers. Well done. It was delivered with 100% battery health which almost certainly means that the phone was opened up and the battery replaced. The likelihood of a 'renewed' 13 Mini arriving with battery health at 100% is slim to none. I assume that they did this because the phone was traded in with < 80% battery health. Amazon advertising states that the phone will arrive with battery health of ≥ 80%. Notably, the battery was recognized by iOS as 'genuine' (thanks TECHMINT). Batteries that are not can lead to various issues, most importantly, safety issues. Look up "how to check if an iPhone battery is genuine". If it isn't, I'd suggest returning it to the supplier. Side note about iPhone battery replacement: If/when you have an iPhone battery replaced, I'd highly recommend scheduling it through Apple. Apple often contracts with third parties to do this in addition to Apple stores. When third parties sign up for this, they're held to a high standard and you're guaranteed to receive a 'genuine' battery. More importantly, if there's a problem you'll have the full weight of Apple behind you to resolve any issues. I'd also suggest reaching out to the supplier before purchase and asking what the battery health will be. In my experience with the iPhone 12 Mini, once you drop into the high 80% range, battery life becomes more noticeable. Note that Apple recommends replacing an iPhone battery when it reaches 80% battery health. I ran two diagnostics to check functions. In both cases, no issues. One of the diagnostics is built into iOS. You'll need iOS 17 or later and not a beta release. Search for 'built in iPhone diagnostic' for instructions. There's another which makes doing this quite a bit easier. From the Apple app store search for 'Phone Doctor Plus'. It's not a diagnostic as much as it's a function check but good for making sure everything works. There's a free and paid version. There are others but these are the only two I've tried. The advertising stated that an MFi certified charging/data cable ships with the phone. Mine shipped with a 3ft braided USB C to Lightning charging cable. No branding or print on the cable, no included documentation, no packaging. It appears similar to what you'll sometimes see without packaging and hanging from peg racks in convenience stores. I have no reason to believe that the provided cable isn't MFi certified and from a reliable manufacturer but without more information, best to use an Apple product or something from an established aftermarket supplier such as Belkin or Anker. Look for 'MFi certified' especially if you want fast charging capability. There are reasons USB C cables can be pricey, especially those designed for high power delivery. Mine shipped without a charger. I'd say the same about a charger as I did about the cable - MFi certified and from a reputable manufacturer - Apple, Belkin, Anker, etc. For the 13 Mini, Apple recommends a minimum of a 20 watt charger for optimal/fast charging . Apple's is about 20 dollars. It's also what Apple recommends for powering *the original* MagSafe accessory. The updated version of the MagSafe charger supports faster charging and according to Apple, a minimum of a 30 watt charger for optimal performance. Some suppliers advertise that a sim card removal tool is included. Mine didn't. If yours shipped with a sim card (mine did not), I'd suggest reading through the pros and cons of SIM vs eSIM. If eSIM meets your needs, I'd recommend removing the SIM and switching to eSIM. Switching to eSIM can be done in your phone's settings. No expertise or hardware required. Although unlikely if buying from an 'Amazon-qualified supplier' (I assume), SIM cards can be compromised. If you need a SIM card, best to get one from your carrier instead of a mystery SIM. The Apple leather case has been my go-to for the last 2-3 iPhones. Very well designed, doesn't add significant bulk, comfortable to grip, no sharp edges and it slips into and out of a pocket easily. The drop protection has proven to be excellent. Great case for all but extreme circumstances. They're relatively pricey so If you're looking to save, there are often Amazon customer returns available. eBay is another good source. The iPhone 12 mini and 13 mini cases are not interchangeable. I tried. The camera lens housings are different. The 12 mini case will not fit the 13 mini. The 13 mini case will fit the 12 mini but there will be a gap on the right side of the lens housing. Not to overstate it but If you're considering both the 12 mini and 13 mini, battery life may be problematic for heavy users. If you have a full size phone with a larger battery at ≥ 90% battery health (guesstimate) and often find yourself scrambling to find a charger, the Mini may not be for you. If you're on the move a lot without convenient charging options, a small power bank (≤ 5000mAh) will bring some peace of mind and a lot of convenience. Great when traveling. Definitely stick with time tested manufacturers. Anker and Belkin sell a wide variety. Note that the TSA only allows powerbanks in carry-ons. Apple discontinued it's iPhone power banks (Magsafe Battery Pack). As of this writing, you can still find them new from third party sources such as Walmart and eBay. Never buy used. There are confirmed and very convincing counterfeits out there so I'd be cautious about which supplier you choose. Look up "how to check if an Apple Magsafe Battery Pack is counterfeit". *Update* Apple reintroduced it's magsafe battery pack now called the iPhone Air MagSafe Battery. It was designed specifically for the iPhone Air and reportedly works with other iPhones - sort of. Not recommended. Fit issues. If you're looking at both the 12 and 13 Minis, the 13 Mini uses an A15 processor which is somewhat more energy efficient and slightly faster. It also has a ~10% larger battery. There are quite a few other differences including an upgraded camera. In day to day use, I found the differences to be negligible. I suspect that most people wouldn't be able to tell the difference without knowing what to look for. Definitely worth reading comparison reviews. Some of the updates will be important for some, less so for others. Search for "iPhone 13 mini vs iPhone 12 mini". If you read only one, Laptopmag.com published a well grounded, real-world comparison, no hype. Long term, the 13 Mini will receive system/feature updates from Apple for about a year longer. This may be the most value added difference. Generally speaking, Apple devices continue to receive security updates beyond the point that they are no longer supported with system/feature updates. Current estimates seem to be late 2027 for system/feature updates and 2030/2031 for security updates. When the security updates stop, best to replace the phone. If Apple's AI (Apple Intelligence) is a feature you want, it isn't supported in the Mini's. You can still use cloud based AI services but without the privacy and security features Apple bakes into it's AI. You'll need a minimum of an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max to use Apple's AI. Happy customer. I'm fully committed to the Mini form factor/dimensions. I carry it all day in a front or back pocket and barely know it's there. Having a phone with more screen, battery and features is nice but after the novelty wears off, having a phone that disappears into a pocket is more important for some of us. Sadly, not enough of us for Apple to justify continued production. When I need to replace it, perhaps Mini's will be back in the menu from Apple. Hope so. Review Title: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking
Review Content: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking up where the prior phone handed off to the latest one. The challenge of course is you have a new phone - and its always a bit steep for the first few days trying to learn the new hardware/software and audit that the used phone does not have some hidden defect that is going to cost you more time and money. So, I'm happy for a few days and then one evening I discover that the bottom speaker (the top earpiece speaker is actually called the receiver) was not working well. scratchy and little to no volume - this had missed my attention entirely. A panic search online revealed Apple 12 speaker problems and them being repaired by Apple - crap! I went to a repair shop the next day, they ran Apple diagnostics on the phone and sure enough - speaker needed to be replaced - $120 for generic parts, $180 for Apple parts - they're not familiar with the Apple repair program (found out later that was for receiver speakers) - so this is half of the cost of the phone. No I'm committed to the new phone, don't want to lose it, but don't want to pay this either. Reach out to seller and explain the issue - they can even confirm the Apple diagnostic through the serial number - They offer $25 refund if I'll keep the phone. - So this tells me that they don't run diagnostics on the phones themselves - or do and hope that people will simply miss small items or accept them once they have sweat equity in the phone - or, it's all honest and by buying/selling a used phone both parties are taking a gamble. I chose to believe the latter. And accepted their offer. And here's the takeaway - the speaker now works - once in a while I might think I hear some scratchy, but unsure due to surrounding conditions. So for now, it's good, we'll see how long it lasts - but if I have to get it repaired - I took a chance - I say take a chance - you might get a perfect phone and save a lot in the meantime - I typically stay a few models behind the curve and benefit from software updates and people abandoning perfectly working phones for the latest models - AT&T typically had new old stock and I took advantage of that, but I have a grandfathered plan that they no longer make good money on, so I'm no longer eligible for that. Review Title: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certifi
Review Content: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certified pre-owned” and ETC are all fancy wording for SECOND HAND, and USED. That said, with high hopes I purchased this device in May 2024 for my birthday, everything seemed to work fine, even though I noticed that the Maximum Battery Capacity was below 90%. —- Now in late January 2025 roughly only 8 months of use and the MBC has fallen to 77%, which has shown extreme degradation in that it cannot hold a charge. In addition, I have noticed that the touch screen is intermittent-Meaning that sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. Sometimes no have to press multiple times and extremely firm—Note that all softer is up to day on the iOS, as well as the Apps used. Also note that I have equipped this phone with a highend sturdy case, which has kept it well protected, although it has not suffered any falls or drops of any kind. Additionally, the screen is and has been protected and covered since the day I received the phone and it still intact with NO cracks or scratches —- All that said, aside from the disappointment of the battery not being at 99% when received and now not holding a charge through the day even with a mid day recharge, I am surprised that I could not get to at least a full 2 years before minor or even major hardware degradation had set in. The question then lies with the company who is selling the phones vs the Apple product itself. I can say ALL my Apple iPhone devices have held the test of time and I’ve never had to upgrade due to hardware, but due to obsoletion. SO, it is my assessment that the company selling the second hand item needs to do a better job checking the devices before resale, as well as fairly pricing it for its age and prior use.-not to mention changing the battery component if it is below 90%. The one, and only good thing I can say was the phone appeared relatively new with little evidence of use meaning just monor scratches on the metal chassis housing, although this goes completely unnoticed as the phone is covered completely with protection. The status of the companies integrity is still up for debate, if they can accommodate my request for a replacement to a newer iPhone model, for which I will pay the difference I will then say happy shopping to all customers, if not, I will say be WEARY of buying used, older model iPhone devices by smaller relatively unknown companies. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 12 Pro, 128GB, Graphite - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller
Review Content: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller. It was roughly $200 more than the regular IPhone 12 that we bought for my son but it was the Pro model and it did have 512k of storage. Due to the positive experience we had with the earlier purchase, I decided to pull the trigger. Fulfillment was great. I had ordered the phone on 7/11 and it was scheduled to arrive on 7/14 but to my surprise it hit my house on 7/13 which was a nice surprise. When I picked up the package I got worried because I could hear and feel something rattling in the box that was shipped in a form fitting padded envelope. To my relief I found the phone to be intact. It arrived with protective plastic on the screen, a SIM port tool, and a lightning charging cable that was loose in the box. Upon inspection I found the screen to be free of scratches or gouges but there is some slight surface marring on a small section of the screen that you have to look for in order to see. The bezel was clean except for a couple of nicks. The worst sign of usage is a chip above the top of the highest camera lens. It’s not huge but you can definitely see it and it looks like a chip in a car windshield since the back of the phone is finished in glass. The only other thing to mention is that there was a bit of what looks like green metal tape that was poking out of the side of the phone between the screen and bezel which I was able to rub off with my fingernail. It looked like the refurb process was not as clean as it could have been. Going into the settings I found that the max battery life was only 85% which was kind of a bummer. Setting up the phone was a breeze with ICloud but I haven’t figured out how to pull down the pictures that resided on my old phone. My apps came over but know I had to re-enter my passwords in most cases. After only a couple of day usage, everything seems to work fine. Amazon gives 90 days to return for any issues. The camera on the pro is a definite improvement over the 7+. Size wise the unit is smaller than the 7+ but the screen is bigger on the 12 since it doesn’t have the home button at the bottom which I keep wanting to press out of habit. Overall the purchase was better than ok. If the phone has another 10% of battery life and the nick on the camera was not present then I would rate the item as excellent. I’ll always wonder if I should have purchased a phone from the other seller that sold a phone in perfect condition. I will update this review should anything major happen with the phone. Review Title: When delivery came, I was waiting by the front door like a little kid during Christmas
Review Content: When delivery came, I was waiting by the front door like a little kid during Christmas. I opened the Amazon box showing 2 items inside and I grabbed the Renewed Premium box and there was no shrink wrap, no sealed close tape to prevent the box from being opened. In my hast, I didn't even record the box opening process. I just flipped open the lid and was shocked to find an empty box with just a charge cable and no iPhone 17 Pro. I looked at the Amazon outside brown box to check for tampering, looked good, one layer of table, not cut open and resealed. I called Amazon Customer service immediately, she said the driver made a mistake and would deliver it the following day (a weekend delivery). My order showed as delivered. - about $1300 and all I had was an emplty box with a USB-C charge cable. That's it. Did I just make the biggest mistake on this on-line order? Why didn't I. record opening the box? I felt bad, and thought driver error??? No way, the outside brown box was sealed. The refurbished box had to have been tampered with in the packing and shipping stage, not during the delivery. I called Amazon Customer Service again, explaining the empty box. They asked for photos which I took shortly after the delivery. They agreed to send a replacement. We got the replacement and were quite happy with it's like new quality. No signs of use, no nics or scratches and it's battery was at 100% capacity with I think 1 cycle on it. Amazon came through with a great replacement. It took several hours to restore and then add it to our account. But all works great now. So, it was a little scary with no product in an empty box, but Amazon Customer Service (my second - third calls) did fix the order and it was a great deal. Look at the refurbished details carefully, and video opening the box and the package contents so you have some evidence on what was was actually in the box. Especially if it is not shrink wrapped or sealed with tape. My video of the replacement didn't show the shrink wrapping well in the photo grab of the opening of the shrink wrap. Thanks to my 2nd and 3rd contact of Customer Service to resolve this purchase. And PS the iPHone 17 Pro is awesome and has lot so space to record kids and concerts. Review Title: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here
Review Content: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway. I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering. The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after. The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced. I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there. So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use. RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking
Review Content: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking. There's no such thing as the simple pinch & zoom on it. That particular luxury seems to be found only within the Camera & Picture sections. You'd think it'd at least be within the iBook section but it's not. On most everything Windows or Google, every app is not just touch & activate, but also affords the luxury of pinch & zoom as well as easy swipe & easy app close & dismiss. Can't say that about the Apple iPhone. And for some unknown reason its WiFi also keeps turning itself on. I can't seem to keep it off no matter how often I manually turn it off. For Apple being so USER-FRIENDLY, I cannot at all say that it is. In fact, IT IS ANYTHING BUT USER-FRIENDLY. If the Apple World was so user-friendly, then it would be a very simple and easy transition from the Windows or Google platform to Apple. And I can honestly say it is Not at all simple or easy. I was so hoping it would be as simple & easy as my Windows machine & Android phone, but sadly, it's actually quite maddening. If you enjoy Kindle reads, you'll need to install the app for it. But I can also tell you, Apple's iBook seriously pales in comparison to Kindle. Ironically, the Google Search Engine is installed on Apple's iPhone but Kindle is not. I avoid Google anything & everything as much as can be done. But for Apple to deny Amazon's Kindle Apple on its phones, seems almost a crime. I have yet to install the Kindle reading app or to test out the camera on the iPhone. When I do I'll update my review. But currently I can't say it's anything to brag about. And I most certainly did not expect to see Google's Search Engine/Web Browser on it. Size wise, it's the exact same size as my Sony Xperia Z3v. It still functions quite well. Not perfect, but well enough for me since I have it locked to call, text, Kindle reads & camera. I can easily read, pinch & zoom & highlight my Kindle reads, pictures & text messages on it. Can only do that with pictures on the iPhone. So for it being so great, I actually find it quite limiting. Not because it's an iPhone, but because the Apple creators decided to create a platform that is quite complex and extremely arduous to use. Apple created its own "language" that must be learned in order to navigate the complexities of its Eco-system. Even now, trying to login to the Apple App Store, no keyboard appears so I can actually install Apps necessary for my personal use. Yet you're required to sign in to it. How can you sign into the App Store when NO KEYBOARD APPEARS TO LET YOU?! So, even if I did not want to use the phone feature, but instead use it as a computer tablet, I cannot because it won't let me login to the App Store. ... Like I said, to anyone new to the Apple world, it's quite a infuriatingly maddening conundrum. If Apple wants to gain new customers and retain them, then Apple needs to change how it operates. And if Apple is supposed to be the safest of all online platforms, then it should not sport Google's web browser. The phone I received was/is like brand new. Operating it though, takes considerable patients as it is quite the learning curve. It should not be so difficult to transition from Windows, Android or Google to Apple. They all made sense to everybody from the moment they came out because they were in simple English and easily understood and simple to navigate because of it. Apple on the other hand, not by a long shot. Even Apple's touchscreen capabilities sorely lacks in comparison. And that's sad. You'd think their touchscreen capabilities would be at least on-par with Windows, Google & Android but it is not. You'd think Apple's touchscreen capabilities might even be better than Windows, Android & Google, but no. Thus far I can find nothing to brag about regarding Apple anything. I was so hoping to find something better about Apple. Instead, I'm greatly disappointed and left seriously frustrated. The iPhone itself came fully charged and appears in brand new condition. It also came with an original Apple Charger.

Review Title: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro
Review Content: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro... and - because of last year's experience - went elsewhere first. What I got from them this time was definitely not what I ordered (it was supposed to be "pristine"... what I got was scratched up junk). So I came back to Amazon, and ordered the only "used-like new" offering on the i13 Pro "list" that day. What I got, well, wasn't (i.e., wasn't "used-like new"). Again. Sigh. (I have a ton of experience with buying "used-like new" stuff from Amazon over the years, and I know what to expect... and this wasn't it.) What I received was a "refurbished-excellent" i13 Pro (the same category as the i13 I ordered last year... which was again, anything but, back then, lol). The category which is is now listed on the order form. (Why would they change the category? When it wasn't what I ordered? -Dunno.) It was... almost... perfect: a few tiny scratches around the lightning port is all a minute examination found wrong (the previous owner had mostly used mag-charging I imagine). And... the battery health - while entirely within the spec for Amazon refurbished (i.e., "80% or greater") - was still a disappointment at only 84%. Still. Cosmetic-wise... acceptable. More than acceptable, even. Agreeably nice... obviously: as I kept it. (Note: I wouldn't review it if I hadn't kept it.) Note: For long term use of any iPhone, to avoid battery related issues, Apple recommends replacing the battery when its below 80% battery health... which repair cost from Apple is about $90 or so... iow, not a big deal. Look, I'm not the target demographic for a new Apple phone anyways; especially their Pro. So sending the phone in for a new battery, especially for what I paid for the 1TB version, is a-okay. And figured into the price. But - other than battery health... and those few tiny [mostly unnoticeable] scratches - I paid quite a bit less (saved a couple of hundred over the "other guys" offerings) at Amazon for a truly ultra-clean i13 Pro - with 1TB capacity - which is in otherwise almost perfect condition. And while its minor flaws render it most certainly NOT in the "used-like new" category... the savings over market costs for a 1TB version rendered my objections to the category moot: it was more than good enough as "refurbished-like new" lol. While YMMV, well... after all... in the final analysis... this one is a keeper. Just keep in mind: all refurb's are "luck of the draw". Amazon is great about their return policy. Take a chance. You'll save money... maybe a bunch of money. Final word: recommend. Review Title: Cuenta con características más que decentes a la fecha pero la batería deja mucho que desear
Review Content: Cuenta con características más que decentes a la fecha pero la batería deja mucho que desear. En cuanto a las cámaras, todas funcionaron muy bien y a la perfección, en la parte trasera funcionan los tres lentes de manera correcta, el flash funciona con normalidad y en este modelo iPhone 13 Pro incluye un sensor LiDAR que ayuda para obtener un mejor enfoque en fotografía y sirve para escanear superficies de manera más precisa, la cámara delantera es buena pero por el precio deja mucho que desear. La aplicación de la cámara es suficiente para el usuario común, tiene varios estilos fotográficos y escaneo de códigos QR de manera nativa pero igual se queda corta en funciones a comparación del modo pro de los Android, lo más destacado es el video, puede grabar en 4K a 60fps y en modo cine en HD a 30fps Su rendimiento en juegos es formidable y puede mover cualquiera en gráficos ultra, altos o medios de manera muy decente, su rendimiento en otras aplicaciones de productividad es decente y te permitirá trabajar sin problemas. Su procesador A15 Bionic es formidable pero no contará con Apple intelligence, por lo que no tiene ni obtendrá mejoras de inteligencia artificial con actualizaciones. La batería es el único inconveniente en este dispositivo, sobretodo cuando tiene menos del 85% porque la duración de la batería se queda corta aunque le den un uso moderado sin mencionar que cuando baja del 80% de vida el sistema reduce el rendimiento y consumo de energía para reducir el desgaste de la pila, por lo que será necesario cambiarla y será recomendable usar cargadores originales para reducir el desgaste de la pila. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 12 Pro Max, 128GB, Pacific Blue - Fully Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I placed my order July 4th and got the phone just 4 days later
Review Content: I placed my order July 4th and got the phone just 4 days later. They shipped FAST! I ordered RENEWED (not Renewed PREMIUM) and I was second guessing myself while awaiting delivery. I worried about the battery health. I was so pleasantly surprised when I checked and saw that it was at 88% health. That is not bad at all. I am more than glad to have the battery replaced eventually when needed considering I saved hundreds of dollars buying a previously used phone AND also sold my old iPhone 8 Plus on eBay. It's only $89 for Apple to replace the battery which is, to me, a good deal considering how many years they last. I'm not bothering to share any photos of the phone itself because there are plenty of those in other reviews here. The phone is virtually flawless. A few very minor scratches around the edges, but I don't care about that. It's covered by the Otterbox case I have it in. Another note is that it was delivered with a tempered glass screen protector already installed. I replaced it with a new one, but it just goes to show they think of everything. They could have removed it but it was a little extra protection while it was in transit. I've been doing my best (and will continue) to try every single feature of the phone before the warranty is up to make sure I don't have any surprises down the road, but I am confident this is going to be my 'new' baby for the next 3 to 4 years. That's about how long I keep a phone before upgrading. I honestly would have kept my old iPhone 8 Plus if not for the fact that I couldn't get iOS 17 on it and I loved the new features of the operating system upgrade. I also wanted a better camera. The sound quality is excellent. the touch screen is completely responsive and I LOVE the beautiful blue color. I implore you to take a chance on renewed/refurbished devices. I have been buying 'like new' devices for decades now and I am rarely disappointed. Any minor aggravations I've encountered have been generously offset by the money I've saved. I always stay a few models behind the newest to get the most savings. Oh! One more thing. If you Google it, many complain of how long it takes the iPhone 12 models to charge. I had the same complaint initially but I just stopped using my convenient bedside USB hub and started using the Anker 60W PIQ wall charger I keep in my living room. That DRAMATICALLY decreased the time it takes to charge. I bought a super long cord here on Amazon so I can charge from a distance and that's all it took. The Anker 60W PIQ charger (also here on Amazon) is lightning fast compared to standard chargers.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100
Review Content: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100 more than the renewed price but for that you get an item whose battery is at least at 90% capacity relative to a new one and instead of a 90 day warranty you get a year warranty and a year to return the item. For less than $100 I thought that was definitely worth it. However the first iPhone 12 pro they sent me had a battery that was at 85% capacity which really pissed me off because I felt cheated so I returned it and purchased it again and I'm glad I did because the 2nd ones battery was at 100% capacity and for all intents and purposes it was a brand new phone at a used price. Granted it's still really expensive it was $900 before tax but I got this to be future proof at least for the next several years. This is my first iPhone before I was all android phones but it seemed like every year I was having to buy another phone because something out of my control always happened but my parents still had their iPhone 8 that they bought new and it was still working perfectly. I haven't had this phone for more than a few days but so far I'm very impressed with it. The facial recognition capabilities are so good. My phone can recognize me when I'm in a dark room whereas my Samsung tablet can't recognize my face without all the lights on. One feature this phone doesn't have that really surprised me was that there is no built in fingerprint scanner and I think that was a mistake on apple's part. The battery is supposed to only last 21 hours but a full charge is lasting me a little over 2 days. The screen is gorgeous is it HDR Dolby Vision and HLG compatible and not even my 4k tv supports all of those so it makes streaming look brilliant. You can see every detail even though the screen is 6.7inches. it seems like everyday I'm finding out a new function that this phone has granted a lot them I'll never use because I don't use my phone that way but it's cool to know that if I wanted to I could if I so choosed. I guess I'll stop my review here because you get the gist and I hate it when people on Amazon beat a dead horse and I don't want to be one of those so Amazon renewed premium is a worthwhile program and the iPhone 12 pro max is an awesome phone that's worth the investment. Review Title: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected
Review Content: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected. My phone was put into what seemed like a generic Android phone box, which, I’ll let you know damn near gave me a heart attack when I opened. Inside were a few things. An Amazon renewed card and one other thing I can’t remember- as well as the phone (obviously) and a charger and charging brick. Charger and charging brick are standard but the cable feels pretty nice and the brick is a good size. Standard plastic holder inside. Nothing more, nothing less. No complaints. For the actual phone, it was inside of a plastic zip bag. The bag itself was scratched up so it was difficult to see the phone inside until i took it out. The first thing I did when I took it out was inspect it for damage. I was completely ready to pack it back up and send it back- but I was pleasantly surprised. The phone had very little cosmetic damage, just some scratches on the frame (my case covers it anyways, so it doesn’t matter to me) and literally no screen damage- besides a little scratch on the upper right corner near the bezel. And you have to remember these phones are used, so I didn’t feel a need to dock a star for that, since you can only see the scratch when the screen is off and light is being reflected onto it. Overall, 9.5/10 for cosmetics. Then, the battery. My particular phone came with 80% battery health, which I personally don’t mind. I have the means to be able to get it replaced when the time comes, and to be honest was a relief after my last IPhone 11 from another seller had 100% battery health, just for it to be a non-Apple battery and cause all sorts of problems. Overall, I have no complaints with this phone. It’s in great condition in my book. Mic, speakers, cameras, haptics, everything (as far as I’ve been using it) has been in perfect order. Based on other reviews, whatever phone you get from this seller honestly depends on luck. It’s trivial, and that should never be the case, but if you can, I’d say take the risk. Worse case scenario you return it and get a full refund and try again. Overall, I’m very happy with my purchase. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 11 Pro, 256GB, Space Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine
Review Content: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. After a week and a half of going round and round with our phone carrier, we finally figured out the phone was not fully unlocked as the listing had set. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”! Review Title: Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery l
Review Content: Update (12/15/23): Ordered a 5th Amazon Premium Renewed phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max), and the battery life, which should be above 90%, is actually 88%. Update (3/28/23): After lengthy discussions with Amazon, they will not honor the 90% battery guarantee stated on the Amazon Premium Renewed page, because it is "not stated on the Amazon invoice". 1-star, no longer recommended. Update (2/1/23): Ran into some issues, probably things that should be checked upon receipt of a renewed or premium renewed product: 1) battery life [below advertised 80 or 90%], 2) parts replaced, either with genuine or non-genuine Apple parts, 3) overall functionality [defective charging port]. Reducing overall rating to 4-stars. Summary: Upgrading from an iPhone 7 plus, and decided I would go with the 11 Pro Max version. I was on the fence whether the extra money for the premium renewed is worth it, so will be discussing what I considered. Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%. Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up. Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only. Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Which you chose would depend on individual financial and personal factors. Apple iPhone 11 Pro Max, US Version, 256GB, Midnight - Unlocked (Renewed)

Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 8 [GPS, 41mm] - Midnight Aluminum Case with Midnight Sport Band, S/M (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada
Review Content: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada. Debería estar catalogado como "Bueno" o "Regular", porque siendo sinceros, sí tiene rayones bastante perceptibles que incluso se sienten al pasar el dedo. Entiendo que es un producto reacondicionado; el problema es que lo venden como “Excelente” y no debería ser así. En cuanto a funcionalidad, llegó impecable. Todo funciona sin problema y la salud de la batería llegó al 87%. En las fotos que agregué se puede ver que desconecté el reloj a las 11:40 a.m. y para las 11:41 p.m. aún tenía el 48% de batería restante. Esto, claramente, con la pantalla siempre activa (AOD) apagada. Con el AOD encendido noté que la batería sí se descarga muchísimo más rápido; le calculo que en vez del 48%, a esa misma hora me habría quedado un 18% o incluso menos. Algo que no me gustó para nada es el cargador genérico incluido. Supuestamente es de la marca Steren, aunque lo dudo, porque la verdad se siente de muy mala calidad (como un cargador muy barato de los que ves en el tianguis). Tardó más de una hora solo en lograr encender el reloj, ya que el equipo llegó con la batería completamente muerta. Llegué incluso a pensar que el reloj estaba defectuoso porque no encendía, pero después de un largo rato por fin lo hizo. Este cargador es de muy baja potencia y provoca que el reloj se caliente bastante; la carga de 0 a 100% tomó más de 2 horas. Si consigues el cable de carga rápida original de Apple, este modelo se carga por completo en unos 45 minutos, ya que el Series 8 sí soporta esta tecnología (me parece que está disponible del Series 7 en adelante). Conclusión: Sí recomiendo la compra (lo compré por un precio de $3,530.27 MXN), pero hagan la inversión de adquirir el cable original (cuesta $649 MXN) para que puedan aprovechar la carga rápida y no tengan que estar esperando más de 2 horas. Por mi parte, aún estoy indeciso sobre si regresarlo o quedármelo, únicamente por los rayones, ya que se perciben demasiado, si no hubiese sido una excelente compra. Bueno, esa fue mi experiencia espero y les sirva.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Being able to track sleep all night and wake up without needing a "panic charge" to get through the workday is a game-changer.

Review Title: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery
Review Content: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive. The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received. I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened. The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process! After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again. Review Title: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto
Review Content: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto. Veniamo all'oggetto della recensione: l'iphone. Una volta tirato fuori dall'orrenda bustina di plastica che lo conteneva, l'ho accuratamente ispezionato rilevando un piccolo segno marcato (circa 1x1 mm) nella parte superiore sinistra dello schermo, dove il display si unisce al notch. A questo si aggiunge un piccolissimo segno (non so come altro definirlo) tra lo schermo e la scocca, nella parte inferiore sinistra. Entrambi i segni sono pressocchè invisibili ad una prima occhiata, occorre esaminare con cura il telefono per rilevarli. Il resto (scocca, schermo, bordi, ecc) è come nuovo. Amazon Renewed dichiara che il telefono "non presenta imperfezioni estetiche visibili tenendo il prodotto a una distanza di 30 centimetri", e direi che la promessa è stata assolutamente mantenuta, ben oltre le aspettative. Esaurita la parte estetica, accendiamo il telefono: l'avvio è immediato, i colori, la luminosità e la presenza dell'opzione True Tone mi fanno pensare che il display è originale Apple, difatti la mancanza del True Tone è solitamente indice di un display non originale o quantomeno più economico di quelli normalmente usati da Apple. Anche il codice IMEI riportato fisicamente sul "cassettino" della Sim corrisponde a quello indicato nelle informazioni del telefono, cosa che mi permette di ipotizzare che il telefono non è il risultato di un assemblaggio di più pezzi provenienti da altri telefoni. La configurazione è avvenuta senza difficoltà e dopo un accurato test di tutta la sensoristica e delle varie parti (Face Id, prossimità, luminosità, touch & 3d touch, giroscopi, tasto muto, volume, power, flash, ricarica wireless, altoparlanti, ecc ecc) non ho rilevato malfunzionamenti o problemi di alcun genere. Il telefono è arrivato con iOs 14.8, versione che se non ricordo male è stata rilasciata intorno a settembre 2021. Analizzando il seriale è possibile determinare l'anno di produzione: il mio nuovo amico risulta essere stato assemblato a Chengdu intorno alla seconda metà di settembre 2018. Facendo due conti, il telefono è rimasto "in giro" da settembre 2018 a settembre 2021, poi non è stato più aggiornato e quindi presumo utilizzato. La batteria presenta una capacità massima dell'80%, in linea a quanto indicato nelle condizioni del prodotto su Amazon. Di sicuro è stato usato non poco, ma il fatto che possa leggere quel valore è un altro ottimo indicatore, significa infatti che la batteria è ancora quella originale, altresì avrei un avviso di "batteria non originale". La scocca posteriore è priva del marchio CE, che di solito identifica i telefoni nati per il mercato Europeo. Ma niente paura, in questo caso significa solo che questo telefono era originariamente destinato al mercato americano o asiatico. Tuttavia, poichè la fotocamera non produce il rumore dello scatto quando è in modalità silenziosa, propendo per il mercato USA. In quello cinese infatti, se non è cambiato qualcosa, i telefoni devono per legge emettere sempre il rumore dello scatto fotografico, così da impedire scatti "rubati". Dura lex, sed lex! Infine faccio una delle ultime ma più importanti prove, vado sul sito Apple e tramite codice seriale verifico la garanzia: e qui ecco la sorpresa (bella)! Non solo il prodotto è regolare, non ci sono allarmi e il seriale è corretto, ma risulto addirittura coperto dall'AppleCare+ fino al 17 di questo mese, mica male :-). Concludo (finalmente, direte voi!): in questo momento sono estremamente contento del mio acquisto, l'iphone è praticamente nuovo e funziona bene. Direi un bel 5 stelle tanto ad Amazon quanto al venditore NEGOZIOREALE, che hanno superato le mie aspettative. Se state leggendo questa recensione, e non importa quando, significa che il telefono sta continuando a funzionare bene. Al primo accenno di problema state sicuri che verrò subito qui ad aggiornare la mia recensione. Review Title: The differences between this and the higher-end models were things I didn’t need (like slightly fast
Review Content: The differences between this and the higher-end models were things I didn’t need (like slightly faster battery charging time, more time between charges, ECG app, SpO2 sensor, water resistance, etc.). I like the wide array of watch faces and customization options for most of them. My personal favorite is the one that includes the option for a 5-hour weather forecast. If you install other faces, you can easily switch between them directly from the watch. I have one with a second hand ready to swipe to for times when I want or need that. One of my favorite features is the ability to set and name alarms by speaking it: “set alarm at 1pm to start getting ready for appointment.” And likewise set and name countdown timers: “set timer to check laundry in 1 hour.” I use this often and it works better than it does on even the iPhone or iPad. The one feature that justified the price for me was the crash/fall detection and emergency SOS. I will be 70 next year and although I’ve never had an issue that required any of this so far (knock on wood), you never know. I was originally not thrilled that I’d have to charge it every day instead of having it last several days (like my Fitbits did). But I found that I easily get thru a full day (plus) after an hour of charge time. So now I just set an alarm to remind me to charge it every night before bed, so now it’s a habit and no problem. That said, the documentation says it runs up to 18 hours on a full charge so I’m not sure how I manage over 24 hours without even resorting to low-power mode. From what I understand, the 18 hour figure is ‘typical use’ and I guess don’t use it ‘typically.’: I don’t use it for music or phone calls, I have the display on the lowest brightness (which is plenty bright), and I don’t use the “always on” setting for the display. So no complaints there! The Health app on the iPhone that interfaces with the watch could be more organized, but the watch itself certainly does more than a standard watch and does many of those things easily — once you know how. One of the things I truly dislike is the silicone band, but that applied to the Fitbit as well. I find them all intensely uncomfortable, too fiddly to put on and take off, and the Apple one pinches me every time I slip the tail end of the strap into the slot that goes under the band. The bands also look too wide on my narrow wrist. But it was simple to find something better on Amazon for everyday wear as well as a band for dressier occasions. They are also a lot easier to swap out than the mechanism on the last two Fitbit watches I had. It’s still a pretty darn big watch, but if it wasn’t, it wouldn’t be as useful either. And it only took me about a week to get used to the size which was faster than I expected. I’ve been using it for almost 3 weeks now and have been very happy with it. Review Content: Returned the watch. The microphone intermittently functioned, the scratches were bothering me, and new watches are only $100 more than this beat up thing. First thing I had to do was clean off the former user’s grime that coated the watch back (yuck!). This took some soap, water, and a toothbrush to clean out the little crevices. Screen and case came with minor scratches overall, with one more annoying, more pronounced screen scratch that really bugs me. Battery was completely depleted, which is not good for lithium batteries. C’mon, for the money you could at least clean and charge the thing! It’s not in terrible shape, but very clearly used. It certainly was not refurbished in any way that I can tell. Imagine buying the watch from your mom after she wore it for a year and you get the idea about my watch’s condition. Not abused, but certainly used. I’m torn. This was not a great purchase, and I’m left wondering if its worth the $150 less than new price. Hard to say. Just don’t believe the product description claiming “appears new” because that is far from the truth. Set your expectations accordingly if you purchase from the “Camera Guyz”. They just take the watch, toss it in a nondescript box with whatever knockoff bits they have laying around, and mail it to you. Look, you’re still paying a lot of money, so there’s no reason not to expect a quality product. Amazon says I have a 90 day warranty, so there’s time (accidental pun) to evaluate it further. Yes it works. Yes, I will eventually add more wear and tear to the watch when wearing. Yes, the “appears new” description is complete fiction. Overall value is debatable. One star for inaccurate condition description and an annoying screen scratch. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation) (Renewed Premium) : Electronics
Review Title: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program
Review Content: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program. I'm not bought into the Apple ecosystem and have no plans to do so, but I won a pair of these at a work event, and they changed my life. Seriously I'm so much more productive because I don't have to listen to the loud project manager sitting next to me on calls all day - that's how good the active noise canceling is. If that's what you're looking for in a pair of earbuds, I've tried and failed to find anything comparable that didn't sacrifice on some other criterion (battery life first and foremost). But here's the deal about the Amazon Renewal thing... I got another pair of honest-to-goodness AirPod Pros in perfect condition with all the accessories at a sizeable discount (though as I write this the same product sold by Apple is discounted down to $190, which is what I paid for this pair :) ). While Amazon isn't my favorite company, and I've had both good and bad experiences with it, I'm happy to help reduce their (and by extension, other companies') environmental footprint by buying a perfectly good product at a cheaper rate just because somebody else's expectations of it weren't met. The packaging of all the accessories was great, the product itself was, as mentioned, indistinguishable from a brand-new set, and I was incredibly happy with them. Now, after finding out that my wife is one of the unfortunate people who are susceptible to vertigo from using noise-canceling headphones, it didn't make sense for us to have 2 pairs, so I decided to return the set I bought Renewed. After a little bit of uncertainty around the return process (the UPS driver will bring a printed label for my otherwise unlabeled package? And I wasn't actually present when he picked it up, so I had to take it on faith that they did, in fact, do that rather than just swiping the box...), I'm getting my full refund, and presumably, somebody else will become the new owner of this nearly-pristine product which reduced Apple's demand for more product to be created by 2 units (so far). In my mind, this program is a win for everyone (possible exceptions of Apple, and employees of Amazon) and the environment. I know what goes into electronics manufacturing (and what comes out other than products), so I'm really glad to see this happening. Super glad Amazon does all this.
